items.caption: SteuerboxHub only captures the §14a EnWG control signal from the grid operator and publishes it via SBH_GetState. It does not control anything itself; the EMS derives setpoints from it for the device hubs.
Two independent axes: “Load” (limiting controllable consumers such as wallbox, heat pump, storage) and “Feed-in” (reducing PV feed-in; self-consumption and battery charging are not affected).

Contacts path: the target value (loadPMin) does NOT come from the hardware and has to be configured here — with the simultaneity factor calculator when several controllable consumers share the same contact.

Important: SteuerboxHub does not detect any hardware automatically. The input variables must already exist — created by a separate IO/GPIO module or a Modbus digitizer (e.g. ADAM module, Shelly) that turns the physical contact of the control box into a Symcon variable. Here you only link an existing variable.
The load axis and the feed-in axis are independently optional — it is enough to link only the input variable(s) you actually have. At least one of the two must be configured.
Feed-in side: real FNN control boxes often report the 0/30/60 % steps through three separate contacts (W3/S1/S2) instead of a single trigger — both variants can be selected.

EEBUS path: the NRG-Stack EEBUS Gateway (a separate module) holds the certificate, the pairing and the connection to the control box. The “EEBUS connector” from this module, which links SteuerboxHub to the gateway, attaches to it (button in the EEBUS section). The control box writes limits in watts for consumption (LPC) and feed-in (LPP), optionally time-limited. If its heartbeat is missing for more than 120 s, the failsafe limits apply until it sends a new limit or the minimum duration (2 to 24 h) has elapsed.

Simultaneity factor calculator (BNetzA formula)

Pmin,14a = 4.2 kW + (n-1) × GZF × 4.2 kW — for several controllable consumption devices (e.g. wallbox, heat pump, air conditioner, storage above 4.2 kW) on this contact. If the value is 0, the simultaneity factor (GZF) is determined automatically from the BNetzA table (0.80 for 2 devices, falling to 0.45 from 9 devices).

Classic ripple control receiver (RCR) four-step scheme 0/30/60/100 %, as used by many grid operators and control boxes regardless of manufacturer. In the §14a variant the §14a signal replaces the 100 % message: contact inactive = no curtailment (100 %), contact active = load limit in effect. Only the input variable(s) are linked here (see note above) — the make of the control box or digitizer does not matter.
